en: The Scripture on the Dharani of the Great Envoy, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci, a Śramaṇa from the Kingdom of South India.
At that time, Vināyaka gathered a great assembly at Mount Kīla; Brahmā himself...
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and others,
along with immeasurable billions of spirits and deities,
rose from their seats, prostrated themselves in homage, and addressed Mahādeva, saying:
I now wish to speak a one-syllable mantra, which says:
"Benefiting sentient beings.
I only pray that you will grant your approval and listen to what I say.
The devas exclaimed, "Excellent, excellent! It is as you have said.
Vināyakas, upon hearing this, were filled with joy and leaped for gladness.
They then uttered the one-syllable mantra of the Vināyakas, saying: VĪM!

Oṃ kha kha khāhi oṃ ha hūṃ phaṭ. "Kha" is the mantra of the body; "khāhi" is the mantra of the crown; "oṃ" is the mantra of the hair; "ha" is the mantra of the heart; "hūṃ" is the mantra of the armor; "phaṭ" is the mantra of subjugation. Recite the syllable "phaṭ" three times. "Vajra" refers to the eyes of the Vināyakas; "vajra" refers to the seat of the Vināyakas. "Oṃ" is for the sake of benefit; "khāhi" is for the purpose of swift punishment; "ha" is for the purpose of causing strife; "kha" is for the purpose of inflicting retribution; "phaṭ" is for the purpose of restraining all things; and the calling of the syllable "hūṃ" is for the purpose of destruction. Having recited "vajra" twice, the single-syllable mantra of binding is proclaimed. After this, the ritual of the maṇḍala is explained.
If one wishes to perform this rite or its image-dharma (pratirūpa-dharma),
one should do so on the fourth day of the waxing moon;
this is the day of accomplishment.
Take *agaru* wood, white sandalwood, or *kṛmuka* wood— one finger-breadth in length—
and carve it into the form of a four-armed deity wearing an insect-skin garment and a crown of seven precious gems upon its head.
The right hand holds a battle-axe;
the lower right hand holds a *hlādana-gaṇḍikā* (joy-bowl).
The left hand grasps a staff; the lower left hand grasps a tusk.
Its head is like that of an elephant;
its left tusk is broken, and it encircles [the prey] with its trunk,
assuming the posture for seizing the *ānandamaṇḍala*.
Adorned from head to toe with various necklaces and ornaments,
she draped a white cord over her right shoulder and across her upper chest;
her feet rested upon a mountain of gold.
Take a silver casket and place therein various kinds of incense, lamps, food, and drink as offerings.
Recite the mantra before it while regularly consuming milk,
or practicing breath-retention (*vāyu*), or eating sesame, wheat, or vegetables.
Recite this single mantra three times daily until it fills the mind;
after four months, construct a mandala measuring four cubits on each side,
and in its center, draw the form of a four-petaled lotus flower.
On the eastern petal of the lotus,
draw the syllable Oṃ; on the western [petal], the syllable Hrīḥ.
The character *Namo* is on the south;
on the leaf facing north, draw the character *Hūṃ*.
For the performance of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*), use *Hūṃ*.
For the protection of the body, use the syllable *phaṭ*.
Outside the lotus, draw the various devas, yakṣas, mātṛs, and others, as well as the mantras of the sun and moon deities.
Outside the maṇḍala, draw the daughters of the four world-protecting kings (*lokapāla*).
Each shall return to its original position.
Take seven leaves of *bodhi* and lotus;
spread the aforementioned leaves upon a lotus flower and place the casket thereon.
Thereafter, take black sesame seeds and cast them into the fire;
recite the mantra once for each seed until eight thousand repetitions are complete.
Then, with the right hand, press down upon the *kośa* (seal-box) within the mandala.
If a sound is produced within, one knows that the rite has been effective.
Thereafter, at a place where there is conflict, take the aforementioned casket and wear it upon your head;
you will easily prevail in the dispute.
Furthermore, regarding the method for summoning others: take a hollowed-out vessel;
by holding a staff in the right hand, one will succeed in all undertakings.
Furthermore, regarding the method for gambling: [the same applies].
Taking an image and tying it to the right foot, one will achieve victory in gambling.
Furthermore, another method: if one wishes to pursue an enemy, take white mustard seeds together with salt.
Take white mustard seed oil and burn it;
by moving the image and making offerings,
one will immediately achieve subjugation and pacification.
It is said that for the Semblance Dharma, one may take a wooden effigy or a piece of wood used for ascetic discipline and carve it according to the previous method.
Furthermore, there is a rite: if one wishes to cause all who have affection and respect [for oneself] to be so inclined, [one should proceed as follows].
Recite the mantra over ox-gallstone one hundred and eight times.
Then, take the ox-gallstone and dot it upon the forehead;
immediately, all will come to love and revere you.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause all beings to love and respect [them],
they should take the filaments of a white lotus as a wick and burn it with cow’s ghee.
With a mind of right concentration, they should perform offerings as before.
Recite the incantation over charcoal ash and ink one hundred and eight times,
then apply it to the eyes;
all that one sees will be loved and respected.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one is in a place where there is fear of wicked bandits, enemies,
or ferocious beasts, one should take the left hand in a fist and press the thumb of the right hand against the palm to form a staff.
Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times;
all evil persons will be driven far away.
If there is anyone who constantly recites this mantra, [they shall be protected].
All people who see him will love and revere him.
Furthermore, as for the method for subjugating people:
take salt and recite the mantra over it once before burning it each time.
Recite this one thousand and eight times,
while also calling out that person's name;
by the seventh day, they will be subdued.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to expel an enemy or cause them to fall into strife and discord,
one should take a fragment of armor and draw the figure of that person upon it.
And having written down their names,
one takes an iron staff before the image and strikes their body with it;
by reciting the mantra for a full seven days, one will achieve success.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to summon a person back,
one should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times before the image three times each day.
One should smear the ground with moist cow dung to form its shape,
or take colored silk and paint its form upon it; then,
take branches from the *kṣīravṛkṣa* tree.
If one maintains this for a full seven days, one will immediately attain success.
If one wishes to remove [impurities] and wash an image with clarified butter (*sarpis*), one will succeed.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one desires to cause others to love and respect [the practitioner], [one should perform this].
Recite the mantra over the body, the confectionery, the medicine, and the food one hundred and eight times.
When calling the person's name while eating, that person will immediately come.
Furthermore, regarding the method for summoning a person:
Take a rope and bind the right hand of the image;
recite the mantra one thousand and eight times while calling out the person's name for up to seven days.
Each of those people will then be bound and come forth.
Furthermore, there is another method: take *vetasa* wood and kindle a fire.
Recite the mantra once for each oblation of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) and offer it into the fire.
Perform this one thousand and eight times until the seventh day.
All people who see him will love and respect him.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue a person,
take water before the image and recite the mantra over it seven times.
If one calls out that person's name, they will come immediately.
Furthermore, as a method for seeking power and wealth,
take the filaments of a lotus flower.
Recite the mantra once for each incense offering, three times a day;
when one thousand and eight recitations are completed, or even after seven days have passed, success will be attained.
Furthermore, regarding the method for subjugating others:
Take the powder of *tila* seeds.
Taking cow’s milk, recite the mantra once over it and burn it before the image.
When seven days have been completed, one will obtain [the desired result].

If one wishes to restrain [the deity],
Oṃ vajrarāga jvala mūle svāhā. If one wishes to destroy an enemy by means of this mantra, one should touch the image with the hand; the third eye will immediately be attained.
Oṃ bhadra-durāgaya-lūriya-mūliye svāhā. If one wishes to cause someone to be obstructed, by touching their ear with the hand, they will immediately attain the fourth [stage].
Oṃ mahorakāya mūliye svāhā. Regarding this dhāraṇī rite, if one wishes to subjugate [an opponent], one should touch the fifth part of the image with the hand.
Oṃ vimurakāya mūliye svāhā. Oṃ haṃsukāya mūliye svāhā. This is the sixth [mantra]. Furthermore, there is a rite that causes the body to become drowsy.
By touching the image with one's hand, the mind is immediately attained.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subjugate a person, one should take the image and direct it toward that person’s heart; the mind is then immediately attained.
Use the first mantra.
Furthermore, if one wishes to restrain an enemy,
hold the image with the hand and point it toward that person's eyes.
That itself constitutes the rite of restraint.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause others to love and revere [the image],
one should touch the shoulder of the image with the hand.
Then employ the second mantra.
Furthermore, if one wishes to protect the body,
touch the image with the hand while holding *śara* grass.
One will immediately obtain [the result]. Furthermore, if one wishes to cure the illness of a person,
one should touch the feet of the image with the hand.
He will immediately recover.
Furthermore, regarding the method for wishing to destroy an enemy:
carve the enemy's image out of *agaru* wood and write their name upon it.
Tread upon it with one's feet.
Use the fourth mantra.
Furthermore, regarding the method for subjugating a person:
Take *maṇḍala* flowers and draw the figure of that person,
writing their name upon it and treading upon it with one's feet.
Then, take leaves of *akā* wood mixed with sugar and clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Recite the mantra once for each incense offering, completing one thousand and eight repetitions.
This first mantra has also been used successfully in subduing [malevolent spirits].
Furthermore, there is another method for those who wish to seek wisdom and intelligence.
Recite the Acorus calamus mantra one thousand and eight times,
and then consume it.
Use the fifth mantra.
Furthermore, the names of the eight Vināyakas are spoken:
first is Crooked Nose (Kubja-nāsa),
and second is Single Tusk (Eka-daṃṣṭra).
The third is named Ivory;
the fourth is named Black Head;
the fifth is named Shoulder-Bearer.
The sixth is named Sharp Teeth;
the seventh is named King of Māras;
the eighth is named Smoke-Colored.
If one constantly recollects these names with a sincere heart,
then all dharmas that have been performed will have all transgressions removed and entirely extinguished.
Furthermore, the ritual procedures for the images of the eight Vināyakas are explained:
for the image with the curved nose, one takes ant-hill earth and moistens it to form the shape of the image;
for the single-tusked image, one takes earth from a riverbank and applies it to form the image.
The Black-Headed One with Red Earth takes the roots and soil of the *kaṭphala* tree;
the Demon King Māra takes the roots and soil of the *karañja* tree.
The color of the smoke is like a painting on white plaster.
This is called the rite of the eight Vināyakas;
perform the offerings in their proper sequence.
Furthermore, if yakṣas, gandharvas,
or others wish for someone to accomplish this dharma,
they should make offerings to the yakṣa of that person.
One shall obtain all that is sought.
One should offer worship with incense for curved noses and flowers;
one should offer worship with various foods, drinks, incense, and flowers using a single tusk.
The youth who acts as the messenger is summoned by the second mantra:
Oṃ vākara cunda ādhipataye svāhā. The body of this messenger takes the form of a human being.
One assumes the form of a sheep’s head with ox hooves, holding a staff in the hand and striking the ground with the heels.
Among the realms of ghosts and spirits, this is the most extremely fierce incantation known as the "Yakṣa-Binding Ghost Incantation.
It may also be employed against all other ghosts.
On that very day, it was as described.
If one recites [the mantra] one hundred thousand times over seven days,
if the incantation is applied to medicine given to a person with an illness, they will immediately recover.
One must not eat the meat of the *hugao* ox or similar substances.
Regarding the mantra for binding the boundary in the four directions:
the third [syllable], *ā ā ja ja ra ra*, transforms into a human body.
He then asked for the name of the messenger Vighna named Dada-pi-pi,
recited the mantra in a low voice,
and placed a blade of *kuśa* grass in each of the four directions to establish a boundary.
The fourth is the mantra of the body itself:
Namaḥ pinākine akṣimukhāya | Tadyathā | ajaye 'ñjaye śubhaṇḍite | uṣitakāye svadhāpāyapātasakhāya | Svāhā. To perform this rite, one must first fashion an image.
Alternatively, one may fashion the images using white tin, copper, or wood;
the two bodies of the husband and wife should be carved in a state of union, standing and embracing one another.
They were both fashioned with the heads of elephants and the bodies of humans.
The price for creating these images was not to be returned.
Once the images had been completed...
On the first day of the waxing moon,
within a clean room, use pure cow dung to grind and fashion a circular altar of any desired size.
One should take one *śroṇa* of sesame oil and apply the aforementioned mantra to it.
Furthermore, warm that pure oil one hundred and eight times,
and place it in a clean copper vessel within the warmed oil.
Thereafter, place the image within a copper basin filled with oil and install it inside the altar.
Using a clean copper spoon or ladle,
pour the oil over the crown of the image’s head one hundred and eight times.
Thereafter, every day one shall further recite the mantra over the old oil one hundred and eight times.
Within a single day, one shall sprinkle it seven times:
four times at dawn and three times at noon, totaling seven times.
Performing the ritual in this manner for up to seven days,
whatever one’s heart desires will be accomplished according to one's wishes.
While the oil is being poured, one should repeatedly make vows.
Form balls from parched grain mixed with ghee and honey;
together with radish roots and one cup of sour wine,
offer these as food every day.
One must consume it oneself to obtain its vital power.

The fifth and sixth mantras for the swift-acting spirit-kings (*śīghrakārin-devaputra*) are: *yaksana yakṣana piśācana kūṭayaleḍa yajña kūpandhu hū huṃ ce huṃ huṃ svāhā*. This mantra is known by two names: first, "The Swift-Acting," and second, "The Universal Impeller."
There is no need for many recitations; three or two repetitions suffice. Second, the boundary-binding:
the messenger Ācārya Ācārya transforms into a human body and asks for the name.
Recite the mantra "Ḍepi ḍepi" once for each blade of kusa grass as a protection against the vināyakas;
place them in the four directions to establish the sixth boundary.
Oṃ bhaṭṭārya-gandhāṇḍu-rājñī-namastebhyaḥ piśāca-vināyakebhyaḥ oṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭha kuṣaha svāhā. This is the Piśāca-Vināyaka spell. If the messenger is a Piśāca-Vināyaka...
One must not cause harm or create obstacles for others.
If one wishes to treat malaria, take four stalks of grass about four inches long,
recite the mantra seven times over them, and strike [the patient].
Surround the person suffering from malaria on all four sides at a distance of about four chi each.
Establish the boundary by placing a *kaṭhina* (woolen cloth) upon the grass; the malaria will then be cured.
If the patient does not come, one may take the incantation scroll and carry it back to encircle their body;
the illness will then be cured immediately.
If one wishes to bind the patient, [one should do so].
Wrap it with grass and place it there.
Recite the mantra seven times in secret, and all will be bound.
When one wishes to perform the rite:
Using a bundle of thatch grass as the boundary,
one should then recite the Great Dharani until it is complete;
immediately thereafter, recite the Messenger Dharani seven times.
Regarding the ritual for subduing vināyakas:
whenever a mantra-reciter experiences fear and terror in a dream,
seeing various animals and other evil omens, [this rite should be performed].
One should know that this is because the yakṣa-king Vināyaka is angry;
whether in dreams or upon waking, one should feel shame and remorse,
and must be cautious.
Tomorrow, there will naturally be food and drink with which to express gratitude.
As for the method of expression: one should moisten the ground with water to create an altar.
One may construct an altar two cubits in size, or it is also acceptable for it to be circular and as large as a platter.
Take five steamed buns and three radishes;
roast them until they are cooked,
and when flowers appear, apply more flowers.
Furthermore, burn white resin incense, frankincense, and so forth within the mandala.
The practitioner shall sit to the west of the mandala facing east.
Having recited the mantra of Maheśvara one hundred and eight times, [the ritual proceeds].
"May you depart with shame and remorse," he said. Having spoken thus,
various items were placed upon a tray within the altar.
Go outside and discard it toward the west;
it is also acceptable to discard it toward the northwest.
Recite: "Sarvayakṣarāja āveśa svāhā. Having spoken these words, discard it and immediately return.
The mantra of Maheśvara is: Oṃ vidrāsaṇi pramardani trāsani trambini trambini svāhā. If one recites this one hundred and eight times, the mind will immediately become joyful.
It is not only within dreams that one perceives demonic activities; even while awake, if such things occur, one should immediately perform this dhāraṇī with a focused mind.

The fifth mantra for the Yakṣa King, who is swift and powerful, is as follows: *Yakṣa yakṣa piśācaṃ kūpaṇḍaya śrīdāyaka kūpaṇḍu hu hu phu phu phu svāhā*. One must first recite it three or five times, and not more than that.
All ghosts and spirits were bound.
At that time, Vināyaka led nine thousand eight hundred great ghost kings and traveled throughout the three thousandfold world system.
We possess sovereign supernatural powers through which we travel throughout all directions to protect and serve the Triple Gem;
with great compassion, we have already brought benefit to sentient beings.
They addressed the World-Honored One in unison, saying:
"By virtue of my sovereign supernormal powers, I am named Vinaraṅga;
I am also called Vināyaka."
They are also called Vaimanaka, and they are also called Mahāvinayaka; thus, the names by which the four continents are known differ.
Furthermore, I have other names for when I appear in the world.
Thereupon, by means of supernatural power, he ascended into the void and spoke these verses:
"I possess a subtle and wondrous Dharma, Which is exceedingly rare in the world."
For all sentient beings who uphold [this], their vows shall be fulfilled.
I act in accordance with the ways of the world, yet manifest rare and wondrous deeds within it.
I can grant whatever they wish; for those who seek fame, I bring about the advancement of their official rank.

I shall cause the king to summon those who seek the extraordinary treasures of the world, and those who seek the accumulation of worldly wealth and profit; may their households be abundant with the seven jewels.
For those who seek the beauty of form, they shall make vows that reach even to the void of space.
Do not speak of distance or proximity, nor of noble status or difficulty;
for those whose minds are devoted to me, I shall, in a mere moment,
relieve the suffering of sentient beings— whether they be possessed by spirits, insane, or afflicted with scabies.
When various evils of disease and poison, and hundreds of kinds of harms and afflictions are added upon one,
there is none who is not liberated by reciting my dhāraṇī.
When walking alone in dark and gloomy places, by relying on me, there shall be no fear.
When bandits suddenly invade, I cause them all to bind themselves;
when worldly phenomena clash and assault one another, I cause them all to be subdued.
Thus I dwell in carefree joy, remaining perfectly complete with nothing lacking.
Whatever they think of shall be accomplished; Whatever they desire shall be fully satisfied.
Even if various evils come to invade them, I shall provide protection for all of them.
May I cause them to fulfill their every wish, And may all who dwell here experience auspiciousness and joy.
The dwellings shall all be pure and peaceful; men and women shall attain illustrious fame.
Husbands and wives shall be harmonious and united. Those who uphold me in the highest degree [shall become] kings among men; those who uphold me in the middle degree...
I shall serve as their imperial preceptor; those who uphold even this inferior grade [of my teaching] will possess inexhaustible wealth and honor.
They shall always enjoy mutual delight, never lacking in full satisfaction, with their servants and slaves gathered in vast throngs.
Beautiful women fill the streets and courtyards; He wanders with sovereign ease, appearing and disappearing at will.
Entering and exiting without obstruction, none can fathom him— I, within the three realms, [am such as this].
Having attained mastery through spiritual powers, all those rare and wondrous deeds performed by me in descending into the world— if one were to speak of my capabilities,
they could not be exhausted even throughout an entire kalpa. Retain this dharani of mine.
I shall appear before all of you; husband, wife, and retinue shall always follow and receive my protection.
When I am traveling, if you recite my name, I will arrive immediately whenever you encounter dangerous or difficult places.
In the great oceans and rivers, in deep mountains and perilous passes,
amidst lions, elephants, tigers, and wolves, among venomous insects and malevolent spirits—
may I remain secure and at ease in all these places; and should there be any who would harass me, [may they be subdued].
"His head shall split into seven pieces, yet his lifespan shall be exceedingly long,

As for the mudrā: interlace the little fingers and ring fingers, bending them inward.
Then, with the two middle fingers held upright and crossed,

Place both thumbs against the sides of the index fingers near their first joints,

Having formed the mudrā, he spoke this mantra:

He further addressed the people of the world:
"If there are those who uphold my dhāraṇī,

You should listen attentively and harbor no doubts.

As for those who establish an altar and make offerings a second time:

Having established the altar for ten periods of ten days, continuing until the end of one's life,

For one who thus upholds the Dharma and practices the rite of image-making,
